title: Wicketkeeper Value: What Should Chennai Super Kings Measure Beyond Dismissals?
dek: A wicketkeeper is judged on catches and stumpings, but in modern T20 the bat matters as much as the gloves. Measuring both changes what Chennai Super Kings should look for.
excerpt: Since 2018, Chennai Super Kings' keepers have batted at a strike rate the data can set against the rest of the league's keepers. In T20, a keeper who scores fast is worth more than one who only keeps tidily.

sections.heading: Beyond Dismissals
body: Catches and stumpings are a keeper's visible output, but most chances are routine. In T20, the larger difference between keepers is often what they add with the bat.
CricField identifies a keeper as a fielder who made a stumping for that side in that season, which captures nearly every regular keeper.

sections.heading: With the Gloves
body: Chennai Super Kings' keepers have taken {{ev:wk-mct}} catches and stumpings. Stumpings make up {{ev:wk-share}} of them, against {{ev:wk-lshare}} across the league, a rough sign of how much they stand up to spin.

sections.heading: What Is Not Measured
body: The data does not record dropped chances, byes saved by diving stops, or the value of a keeper's advice on reviews and field settings.
Those are real, but they need video or tracking data to measure.

sections.heading: CricField Verdict: Price the Bat, Check the Gloves
body: Chennai Super Kings should value keepers primarily on batting tempo and role, and use keeping data to rule out weak glovework rather than to rank keepers.
Dropped-chance data would make the glovework side of the judgement far sharper.
